clusters.title: Tell us: did you move to the countryside for retirement and come to regret it?
clusters.neutral_headline: Tell us: did you move to the countryside for retirement and come to regret it

items.title: Tell us: did you move to the countryside for retirement and come to regret it?
items.standfirst: As England’s chief medical officer warns of the challenges of growing older in rural areas, we’d like to hear from people who have struggled with isolation or accessing services and supportEngland’s chief medical officer Chris Whitty has warned of the potential downsides of choosing to spend the later part of your life in a rural area. He urged people to think carefully about the challenges of rural life as they get older, including poor access to healthcare, limited public transport and the risk of becoming isolated or dependent on others.We want to hear from the people people who have experienced these challenges. Did you move to the countryside for your retirement and find it more difficult to access the services and support you need? Are you feeling dependent on others to get around and access amenities, leaving you wishing you’d stayed in a town or city? Or have you moved back to a city, finding rural life too isolating as you become older? Continue reading...

clusters.title: 1 in 2 review – compassionate film about dealing with bowel cancer is a personal plea on behalf of the young
clusters.neutral_headline: 1 in 2 review – compassionate film about dealing with bowel cancer is a...

items.title: 1 in 2 review – compassionate film about dealing with bowel cancer is a personal plea on behalf of the young
items.standfirst: David Wilkinson made this warm, generous documentary of his own treatment, and asks why so many much younger people are getting the same diagnosis‘I am lucky, as I have become old.” That is the pithy, personal summary offered by English film-maker David Wilkinson, whose previous movie was his thoughtful, eloquent film The Marbles, which reopened the case for the restitution of the Parthenon marbles to Greece. Now he reveals that he was in fact battling stage four bowel cancer throughout its making, and this new and very personal film is now about his own condition, a film in which the director is front and centre, speaking candidly to camera in the very midst of his treatment.In fact, 1 in 2 is specifically about his shock and sadness that so many people alongside him in waiting rooms, or online in bowel cancer discussion groups are so young, in their 40s, or 30s, or 20s. Wilkinson makes it his business to give these people a voice, along with the medical professionals in the NHS who are battling to help them. He also wants to find something out: why is something that was once considered an old person’s disease on the rise in younger age groups in developed nations? It appears to be due to diet and lifestyle. Could it be microplastics? There are no clearcut answers. Continue reading...
